questionText: Consider the following snapshot of a system running $n$ concurrent processes. Process $i$ is holding $X_i$ instances of a resource R, $1 \le i \le n$. Assume that all instances of R are currently in use. Further, for all $i$, process $i$ can place a request for at most $Y_i$ additional instances of R while holding the $X_i$ instances it already has. Of the $n$ processes, there are exactly two processes $p$ and $q$ such that $Y_p = Y_q = 0$. Which one of the following conditions guarantees that no other process apart from $p$ and $q$ can complete execution?
options: $X_p + X_q < \text{Min } \{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \neq p, k \neq q\}$
$X_p + X_q < \text{Max } \{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \neq p, k \neq q\}$
$\text{Min } (X_p, X_q) \ge \text{Min } \{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \neq p, k \neq q\}$
$\text{Min } (X_p, X_q) \le \text{Max } \{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k \neq p, k \neq q\}$
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze current state and available resources
All instances of resource R are currently allocated, meaning the initial available count of R is $0$.
Processes $p$ and $q$ have additional requirement $Y_p = 0$ and $Y_q = 0$, meaning neither process requires any additional resources to finish.

Step 2: Determine available resources after $p$ and $q$ execute
Since $p$ and $q$ require $0$ additional instances, both can complete execution and release their held resources $X_p$ and $X_q$.
After $p$ and $q$ finish, the total available resources in the system become $X_p + X_q$.

Step 3: Condition for other processes to execute
Any remaining process $k$ ($k eq p, q$) requires $Y_k$ additional instances to complete.
Process $k$ can execute if $Y_k \le X_p + X_q$.
To guarantee that no other process apart from $p$ and $q$ can complete execution, the requirement $Y_k$ for every remaining process $k$ must be strictly greater than the available resources $X_p + X_q$:
$Y_k > X_p + X_q \quad ext{for all } k eq p, q$

Step 4: Conclusion
For $Y_k > X_p + X_q$ to hold for all $k eq p, q$, the available resources must be strictly less than the minimum additional requirement among all other processes:
$X_p + X_q < ext{Min } \{Y_k \mid 1 \le k \le n, k eq p, k eq q\}$

Hence, option (A) is correct.
